title: Model hot-swap and quantization fallbacks playbook
author: Sofia Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook describes the recommended process for performing a model binary hot-swap in Private deployments with zero-to-minimal user-visible downtime. It includes safe canary rollout steps, KV cache compatibility checks, quantization-fallback policies, and automated verification gates. Use this when promoting a new model version (including quantized variants) to production clusters in customer VPCs or on-prem installations.

Scope

- Applies to model artifacts served by the Redwood runtime on Private deployments (VPC & on-prem).
- Covers both architecture-level decisions and operator step-by-step commands.
- Excludes changes to storage or network topology (covered elsewhere).

Goal and success criteria

- Goal: Replace model vX -> vY on live nodes while maintaining SLOs (p95 latency < 120ms for interactive workloads, error rate < 0.5%).
- Success: 95% of traffic observes no degradation; automated quality checks pass; rollback/recovery time < 10 minutes if a regression is detected.

Prerequisites and assumptions

- Operator has access to the private deployment control plane and can run the release CLI (redwoodctl).
- The model artifact is published to the customer's artifact store and has a verified checksum.
- New model packaging follows the artifact manifest schema (see example below).
- KV cache format compatibility is declared in the model manifest (compatible | migrate_required).
- SRE and customer (if requested) are notified per the customer contract at least 48 hours before rollout.

Model artifact manifest (example)

| field | description | example |
|---|---:|---|
| name | canonical model name | rdl-7b-int8 |
| version | semantic version | 2026-06-01 |
| binary_sha256 | artifact checksum | ab12...ef34 |
| kv_compat | KV cache compatibility flag | compatible |
| quantization_profiles | list of supported quant profiles | int8, int4 |
| fallback_variant | fallback model to use on degradation | rdl-7b-fp16 |

Architecture notes

- Nodes run the Redwood runtime with a two-tier model loader: a controller agent (control-plane sidecar) and per-worker model process.
- KV cache is sharded by tenant and persisted on local SSD; format versioning is enforced via manifest.
- Hot-swap leverages a connection draining circuit: new workers are provisioned with the new model, warmup is applied, small percentage of traffic is routed, then global switch occurs.

High-level strategy

1) Validate artifact and manifest.
2) Deploy model binaries to an isolated canary subset (1–5% traffic).
3) Run deterministic quality and perf checks on canary traffic (synthetic prompts + replay traces).
4) Gradually ramp to 25%, 50%, then 100% with verification gates at each step.
4b) If the manifest indicates kv_compat = migrate_required, perform KV cache migration during the 25% stage.
5) Finalize and retire old binaries once stable for 24 hours.

Safety nets and fallbacks

- Quantization fallback: if the new quantized variant shows a quality regression beyond configured thresholds, traffic is automatically diverted to the fallback_variant via routing policy.
- Circuit breaker: the runtime tracks per-node error rates and latency; nodes exceeding thresholds are automatically taken out of the pool.
- Emergency rollback: keep the old model binary staged on every node for immediate revert.

Pre-deployment checklist

- [ ] Artifact checksum verified and signed.
- [ ] Manifest uploaded to artifact registry.
- [ ] Canary node group defined (labels: deploy-role=canary).
- [ ] Synthetic prompt set created for canary evals (see ./prompt-sets).
- [ ] Monitoring dashboards copied and baseline recorded.

Canary procedure (operator steps)

1) Stage artifact to nodes (no activation):

redwoodctl artifact push --model rdl-7b-int8 --version 2026-06-01 --target-group canary

2) Verify checksums on canary nodes (sample 5 nodes):

redwoodctl node exec --group canary --cmd "sha256sum /opt/redwood/models/rdl-7b-int8.tar.gz"

3) Warmup model process (KV cache priming optional):

redwoodctl node exec --group canary --cmd "systemctl start redwood-model@rdl-7b-int8"
redwoodctl warmup --group canary --prompts-file ./canary-prompts.json --workers 8 --iterations 20

4) Route 1% of production traffic to canary via routing policy: edit routing policy and set traffic allocation.

5) Run automated verification suite (quality + perf):

- Quality: run prompt-set evaluation (BLEU/ROUGE or Redwood eval hooks).
- Perf: p50/p95 token latency, memory, and peak GPU utilization.
- Regression thresholds: quality delta <= 1.5% relative to control; p95 latency change <= 20ms.

6) Observe for 30 minutes. If pass, proceed to ramp (25%). If fail, either fix (redeploy) or rollback.

KV cache migration pattern (if migrate_required)

- Migrate during 25% ramp to limit blast radius. Steps:
  1) Lock writes to the affected tenant shards (short maintenance window).
  2) Snapshot existing KV shards and copy to migration pool.
  3) Run conversion tool on snapshot: redwoodctl kv migrate --from-format v1 --to-format v2 --shard-id <id>
  4) Validate a sample (synthetic prompts) against migrated shard.
  5) Promote migrated shards and unlock writes.

Rolling upgrade (ramp and full switch)

- 25% stage: expand canary group and reroute 25% traffic. Run full verification (3 hours).
- 50% stage: double canary nodes, continue monitoring (6 hours).
- 100% stage: schedule short cutover window (low traffic), drain old model processes and activate new model on remaining nodes.

Activation commands (example)

# Drain old process gracefully on node
redwoodctl node exec --node <node-id> --cmd "redwoodctl model drain --model rdl-7b-fp16 --grace 60"

# Start new model
redwoodctl node exec --node <node-id> --cmd "systemctl start redwood-model@rdl-7b-int8"

Verification and post-cutover checks

- Run smoke tests for 1000 synthetic prompts. All responses must parse and pass required assertions.
- Check SLO telemetry: p95 latency under target and error rate under 0.5% for 2 consecutive hours.
- Spot-check customer-specific prompt sets if provided.
- Confirm KV cache hit rate is within expected range; investigate sudden drops.

Automated rollback flow

Trigger conditions (automated or manual):
- Quality regression > configured threshold.
- Error rate spike > 2x baseline for 10 minutes.
- Sustained latency degradation p95 delta > 100ms for 15 minutes.

Automated rollback steps (runtime policy):
1) Route new-variant traffic -> fallback_variant at the cluster-level (atomic routing change).
2) Mark all new nodes as draining for model process.
3) Re-enable old model binary on nodes (if stopped) using redwoodctl.
4) Run targeted tests against fallback_variant.
5) Raise incident and notify stakeholders.

Manual rollback (operator)

1) redwoodctl routing set --model rdl-7b-int8 --allocation 0 --fallback rdl-7b-fp16
2) redwoodctl node exec --group all --cmd "systemctl stop redwood-model@rdl-7b-int8; systemctl start redwood-model@rdl-7b-fp16"
3) Verify smoke tests and SLOs.

Monitoring, dashboards and alerts

Key metrics to monitor:
- Model-serving p50/p95 token latency (per-model, per-tenant)
- Error rate (5xx/processing-failed)
- Quality regressions (scoring from eval harness)
- KV cache hit ratio and migration progress
- GPU memory pressure and OOM events

Recommended alerts:
- p95 latency > target + 50ms for 5 minutes -> pager to SRE (severity P2)
- Error rate > 1% sustained for 5 minutes -> pager (P1)
- Eval quality drop > threshold -> notify on slack #model-regressions and email owners

Ownership and communication

- Release owner: person who runs the redwoodctl release (Document this in the ticket).
- SRE contact: on-call SRE for the cluster.
- Customer contact: account manager if SLA/contract requires advance notice.
- Post-release: update deployment ticket with verification snapshots and close once stable 24 hours.

Troubleshooting checklist (common failures)

- Symptom: spike in 5xx errors after warmup
  - Check model logs (/var/log/redwood/model-*.log) for OOM or serialization errors.
  - Verify binary integrity and library compatibility.

- Symptom: KV cache hit rate drops to zero
  - Confirm kv_compat flag; examine migration logs (redwoodctl kv status).
  - Re-run migration on a sample shard and validate.

- Symptom: higher hallucination rate in canary
  - Run targeted eval prompts and compare token-level log probabilities.
  - If severe, set immediate routing fallback and open incident.

Appendix A — Example routing policy (YAML)

apiVersion: redwood/v1
kind: RoutingPolicy
metadata:
  name: rdl-7b-int8-rollout
spec:
  model: rdl-7b-int8
  stages:
    - name: canary
      allocation: 0.01
      selectors: {deploy-role: canary}
    - name: ramp25
      allocation: 0.25
    - name: ramp50
      allocation: 0.5
    - name: global
      allocation: 1.0
  fallback: rdl-7b-fp16

Appendix B — Synthetic prompt checklist

- Core intents (50): basic completions and instruction-following
- Edge cases (20): long-context (>4k tokens), truncated prompts
- Safety checks (20): adversarial or policy-sensitive prompts
- Regression probes (10): known customer-critical prompts (redacted)

FAQ

Q: Can we hot-swap across major architecture changes (e.g., llama->transformerX)?
A: Only if the runtime supports binary compatibility and the manifest indicates kv_compat=compatible. Large architecture changes generally require blue-green deployment with a longer maintenance window.

Q: How long should the warmup run be?
A: Typical warmup: 30–120s per worker with 20–50 synthetic prompts. For large models or large KV state, extend accordingly.
